text: **RULED BY hv 2026-08-19, REPLACING THE TWO-REGION DESIGN. `.intentfiles` IS DURABLE STATE: THE RECORD OF WHICH DATABASE ARTEFACTS ALSO HAVE A REALISED FORM ON DISK.** **THE ARCHITECTURE IN ONE LINE, hv's: REALISATION IS DRIVEN FROM `.intentfiles`; COMMANDS CHANGE `.intentfiles`; `organize` REALISES IT.** **_AUTHORED_ WAS vc's WORD AND IT IS WRONG -- hv corrected it before anyone built on it.** It is NOT _never touched by an intent command_: **`st new` ADDS the id, `st done` REMOVES it, `st hydrate`/`st dehydrate` and the ISSUE equivalents do it directly, and a human may edit it by hand.** **THE ONE THING THAT CHANGED FROM THE TWO-REGION DESIGN IS THAT NOTHING RECOMPUTES IT.** There is no derivation from status that overwrites what is there, which is why the protected region is unnecessary: **a write is a CHANGE TO STATE, never a REGENERATION OF IT.** hv: _why isn't the organise operation simply: a) look at .intentfiles, b) hydrate the items in the file, c) dehydrate any previously hydrated items that are no longer in the file._ **THE TWO REGIONS EXISTED ONLY BECAUSE THE FILE WAS MACHINE-GENERATED: if `organize` rewrote the list from status every run, a hand-added line would be wiped, so a protected region was needed. Remove the regeneration and the protected region has nothing to protect against.** **IT ALSO EXPLAINS WHY `intentfiles::render` HAD NO CALLER: the thing it does is not needed.** No function of status, no negative pin, one writer, one source of truth. **THE LIST WINS OVER STATUS: a `completed` or `cancelled` artefact that IS listed stays on disk through `organize`, and a `wip` artefact that is NOT listed is removed by it.** This is the property the pinned region used to buy, and it is now the ordinary behaviour rather than an exception -- **status has no vote at `organize` time at all.** Both directions checked, because a rule that only keeps things cannot be told from one that never removes any.
